title: 1998 AHSME Problem 16
statement: The figure shown is the union of a circle and two semicircles of diameters \(a\) and \(b,\) all of whose centers are collinear. The ratio of the area of the shaded region to that of the unshaded region is

solutions.text: The shaded area is \[ \begin{aligned} &\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac{a+b}{2}\right)^2 +\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac a2\right)^2\\ &\qquad-\frac{\pi}{2}\left(\frac b2\right)^2 =\frac{\pi a(a+b)}4. \end{aligned} \] Similarly, the unshaded area is \(\frac{\pi b(a+b)}{4}.\) Their ratio is \(\frac{a}{b},\) so B is correct.
hints: Express each region using the large semicircle and one small semicircle
Both resulting areas factor a common multiple of \(a+b\)
